1.title: Cache Memory Notes
1.summary: Key ideas about cache hit, cache miss, locality, and set associative cache.
1.text_preview: Cache memory reduces average memory access time by exploiting temporal locality and spatial locality. A cache hit finds data in a nearby cache line, while a cache miss requires fetching it from a lower memory level. Set associative cache balances lookup cost and flexibility.
1.ai_summary: Mock summary: Cache memory improves performance through temporal and spatial locality. Cache hits are fast, while cache misses fetch data from lower memory levels.

cards.answer: Cache memory reduces average memory access time by exploiting temporal locality and spatial locality.

1.title: CPU Pipeline and Hazards
1.summary: Pipeline stages, data hazards, control hazards, and forwarding.
1.text_preview: A CPU pipeline overlaps instruction stages to improve throughput. Data hazards occur when instructions depend on earlier results, while control hazards come from branches. Forwarding and branch prediction reduce some pipeline stalls.
1.ai_summary: Mock summary: CPU pipelining improves instruction throughput by overlapping stages. Data hazards and control hazards can create stalls, which forwarding and branch prediction help reduce.

2.title: Gradient Descent Notes
2.summary: Loss function, gradient descent, learning rate, and model convergence.
2.text_preview: Gradient descent minimizes a loss function by moving model parameters opposite to the gradient. The learning rate controls the step size, and a suitable rate helps the model converge without overshooting.
2.ai_summary: Mock summary: Gradient descent minimizes a loss function by following the negative gradient. The learning rate controls each update and strongly affects convergence.

cards.answer: Gradient descent minimizes a loss function by moving model parameters opposite to the gradient.

cards.answer: The learning rate controls the step size of each parameter update.

cards.question: How would you explain this material in one sentence?
cards.answer: A suitable learning rate helps the model converge without overshooting.

3.title: Linked List Review
3.summary: Nodes, pointers, insertion, deletion, and linked list traversal.
3.text_preview: A linked list stores data in nodes connected by pointers. Insertion and deletion can be efficient when the target node is known, but traversal takes linear time because nodes are not stored contiguously.

3.title: Trees and Graphs Basics
3.summary: Tree traversal, breadth-first search, depth-first search, and graph connections.
3.text_preview: Trees represent hierarchical relationships, while graphs represent general connections. Breadth-first search explores level by level, and depth-first search explores one branch before backtracking.
